## Examples

This in-class file is used for demonstrating individual examples related to this topic and is kept as a persistent record of examples provided during lectures.

## The Data

There are two data sets used for this example;

-   The *iris* data set (that comes with R) that describes the sepal and petal sizes on three species of *Iris*. This is a classic data set found in a wide variety of courses and textbooks and is a great example of having several sample measurements on several individuals in different groups.

```{r}
summary( iris )
```

![Measurements of sepal and petal lengths and width for three species of iris.](https://flickr.com/photo_download.gne?id=52436835869&secret=1804e00ce8&size=w&source=photoPageEngagement){#fig-iris}


## Vectors

A vector is a list of elements that **must** be the same class of variable.  Key skills include, creating, manipulating, changing the values in, and analyzing the contents of `vector` objects.




## Matrices

Matrices are a collection of data types in a 2- or 3-dimensional configuration, often used for mathematical modeling.  Key skills are creating, accessing, and changing values in matrices.



## Lists

Lists are a structure that allows you to have *named* variables. Elements may be of different class and sizes. Key skills are extracting information from list-like objects (mostly from calling functions.)


## Data Frames

A `data.frame` is a dense data container similar to that of a spreadsheet where each column has data of the same type (e.g., Latitude, or Temperature) and each row represents a single record of measurements taken together (same time, same individual, etc.).  The key skills here are creating (mostly loading from file), manipulating, extracting data from, and summarizing data contained in a `data.frame`.  


## Communicating About Data

A main focus for this course is to be able to not only perform data analytics but to effectively communicate these results.  This means that we need to develop skills necessary for including inferences from the data into our narrative.
